requirements.quote: The message header for each MQTT command message contains a fixed header.
requirements.condition: For every MQTT command message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a fixed header in the message header.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized command message can be inspected for the required fixed-header fields.

requirements.quote: Byte 1 Contains the Message Type and Flags (Dup, QoS level, and RETAIN) fields.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding byte 1 of the fixed header.
requirements.required_behavior: Use byte 1 for the Message Type, DUP, QoS level, and RETAIN fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit fields present in the first fixed-header byte can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: Byte 2 (At least one byte) contains the Remaining Length field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the fixed header after byte 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Remaining Length field beginning at byte 2 and use at least one byte for it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode a zero-byte Remaining Length field.
requirements.why_checkable: The location and encoded byte count of Remaining Length are observable on the wire.

requirements.quote: All data values are in big-endian order: higher order bytes precede lower order bytes. A 16-bit word is presented on the wire as Most Significant Byte (MSB), followed by Least Significant Byte (LSB).
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing multibyte data values.
requirements.required_behavior: Place higher-order bytes before lower-order bytes; encode a 16-bit word as MSB followed by LSB.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode multibyte data values in little-endian byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: Known multibyte values can be serialized and their byte order compared with the specified order.

requirements.quote: Message Type Position: byte 1, bits 7-4. Represented as a 4-bit unsigned value.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the Message Type.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Message Type as an unsigned 4-bit value in bits 7-4 of byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The position and width of Message Type can be verified from the first byte.

requirements.quote: Mnemonic Enumeration Description Reserved 0 Reserved CONNECT 1 Client request to connect to Broker CONNACK 2 Connect Acknowledgment PUBLISH 3 Publish message PUBACK 4 Publish Acknowledgment PUBREC 5 Publish Received (assured delivery part 1) PUBREL 6 Publish Release (assured delivery part 2) PUBCOMP 7 Publish Complete (assured delivery part 3) SUBSCRIBE 8 Client Subscribe request SUBACK 9 Subscribe Acknowledgment UNSUBSCRIBE 10 Client Unsubscribe request UNSUBACK 11 Unsubscribe Acknowledgment PINGREQ 12 PING Request PINGRESP 13 PING Response DISCONNECT 14 Client is Disconnecting Reserved 15 Reserved
requirements.condition: When mapping the 4-bit Message Type field to an MQTT command type.
requirements.required_behavior: Map values 1 through 14 respectively to CONNECT, CONNACK, PUBLISH, PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK, PINGREQ, PINGRESP, and DISCONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: Each encoded value can be compared against the enumerated command mapping.

requirements.quote: Mnemonic Enumeration Description Reserved 0 Reserved CONNECT 1 Client request to connect to Broker CONNACK 2 Connect Acknowledgment PUBLISH 3 Publish message PUBACK 4 Publish Acknowledgment PUBREC 5 Publish Received (assured delivery part 1) PUBREL 6 Publish Release (assured delivery part 2) PUBCOMP 7 Publish Complete (assured delivery part 3) SUBSCRIBE 8 Client Subscribe request SUBACK 9 Subscribe Acknowledgment UNSUBSCRIBE 10 Client Unsubscribe request UNSUBACK 11 Unsubscribe Acknowledgment PINGREQ 12 PING Request PINGRESP 13 PING Response DISCONNECT 14 Client is Disconnecting Reserved 15 Reserved
requirements.condition: When interpreting or producing the Message Type field.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat Message Type values 0 and 15 as reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat values 0 or 15 as one of the defined MQTT command types.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify whether the implementation exposes reserved values as defined commands.

requirements.quote: The remaining bits of byte 1 contain the fields DUP, QoS, and RETAIN. The bit positions are encoded to represent the flags as shown in the table below. Bit position Name Description 3 DUP Duplicate delivery 2-1 QoS Quality of Service 0 RETAIN RETAIN flag
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the flags in fixed-header byte 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Place DUP in bit 3, QoS in bits 2-1, and RETAIN in bit 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Each flag's bit position is directly observable in byte 1.

requirements.quote: This flag is set when the client or broker attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: When a client or broker attempts to redeliver a PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A redelivery operation can be induced and the resulting PUBLISH fixed header inspected.

requirements.quote: This applies to messages where the value of QoS is greater than zero (0), and an acknowledgment is required.
requirements.condition: When applying DUP-based PUBLISH redelivery behavior described here.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply that behavior to messages whose QoS is greater than 0 and which require an acknowledgment.
requirements.why_checkable: Redelivery behavior can be tested across QoS values and acknowledgment requirements.

requirements.quote: When the DUP bit is set, the variable header includes a Message ID.
requirements.condition: When the DUP bit is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Message ID in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the Message ID from the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The variable header of a packet with DUP set can be parsed for a Message ID.

requirements.quote: QoS Position: byte 1, bits 2-1.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the QoS field.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the QoS field in bits 2-1 of byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The QoS field's position is directly observable in fixed-header byte 1.

requirements.quote: QoS value bit 2 bit 1 Description 0 0 0 At most once Fire and Forget <=1 1 0 1 At least once Acknowledged delivery >=1 2 1 0 Exactly once Assured delivery =1 3 1 1 Reserved
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a PUBLISH QoS level.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode QoS 0 as bits 00, QoS 1 as bits 01, and QoS 2 as bits 10.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits can be compared with the specified value mapping.

requirements.quote: QoS value bit 2 bit 1 Description 0 0 0 At most once Fire and Forget <=1 1 0 1 At least once Acknowledged delivery >=1 2 1 0 Exactly once Assured delivery =1 3 1 1 Reserved
requirements.condition: When interpreting or producing the QoS field.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat QoS bit pattern 11, value 3, as reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat QoS value 3 as a defined delivery level.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify that bit pattern 11 is not accepted or emitted as a defined QoS level.

requirements.quote: When set, the Retain flag indicates that the broker holds the message, and sends it as an initial message to new subscribers to this topic.
requirements.condition: When a published message has the Retain flag set.
requirements.required_behavior: Have the broker hold the message and send it as an initial message to new subscribers to that topic.
requirements.why_checkable: Publish and subsequent new-subscription behavior can be exercised and observed.

requirements.quote: After sending a SUBSCRIBE message to one or more topics, a subscriber receives a SUBACK message, followed by one message for each newly subscribed topic that has a retained value.
requirements.condition: After a subscriber sends SUBSCRIBE for one or more topics, where newly subscribed topics have retained values.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the subscriber a SUBACK followed by one message for each newly subscribed topic having a retained value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the retained messages before the SUBACK.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet ordering and the number of retained messages can be observed after a subscription.

requirements.quote: The retained value is published from the broker to the subscriber with the Retain flag set and with the same QoS with which it was originally published, and is therefore subject to the usual QoS delivery assurances.
requirements.condition: When a broker publishes a retained value to a subscriber.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Retain flag and use the same QoS with which the value was originally published.
requirements.why_checkable: The delivered retained PUBLISH flags and QoS can be compared with the stored original publication.

requirements.quote: The Retain flag is set in the message to the subscribers, to distinguish it from "live" data so that it is handled appropriately by the subscriber.
requirements.condition: When sending a retained message to subscribers.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Retain flag in the message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the retained message with the Retain flag clear.
requirements.why_checkable: The outgoing retained message's fixed-header Retain bit can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Represents the number of bytes remaining within the current message, including data in the variable header and the payload.
requirements.condition: When calculating or interpreting Remaining Length.
requirements.required_behavior: Set its value to the combined number of bytes in the variable header and payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded value can be compared with the actual variable-header and payload byte count.

requirements.quote: The variable length encoding scheme uses a single byte for messages up to 127 bytes long.
requirements.condition: When Remaining Length is between 0 and 127 inclusive.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Remaining Length in one byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The number of bytes used for values through 127 can be measured.

requirements.quote: Seven bits of each byte encode the Remaining Length data, and the eighth bit indicates any following bytes in the representation.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding each Remaining Length byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Use seven bits for value data and the eighth bit as the continuation indicator for following bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Each byte's low seven bits and high continuation bit can be inspected independently.

requirements.quote: The number 321 decimal (=128x2 + 65) is encoded as two bytes, least significant first.
requirements.condition: When encoding multibyte Remaining Length values.
requirements.required_behavior: Emit base-128 digits least significant first.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Emit multibyte Remaining Length digits most significant first.
requirements.why_checkable: A value such as 321 can be encoded and its digit order inspected.

requirements.quote: The first byte is 2+128 = 130. Note that the top bit is set to indicate at least one following byte. The second byte is 65.
requirements.condition: When encoding Remaining Length value 321.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as decimal bytes 130 and 65, in that order, with the first byte's top bit set.
requirements.why_checkable: The exact two-byte encoding can be compared byte-for-byte.

requirements.quote: The protocol limits the number of bytes in the representation to a maximum of four.
requirements.condition: When encoding or accepting a Remaining Length representation.
requirements.required_behavior: Use no more than four bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Emit or accept a Remaining Length representation containing more than four bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoders and parsers can be tested with representations at and beyond four bytes.

requirements.quote: This allows applications to send messages of up to 268 435 455 (256 MB).
requirements.condition: When determining the maximum representable MQTT message remainder.
requirements.required_behavior: Support Remaining Length values up to 268435455 bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode a Remaining Length value greater than 268435455.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests can exercise the maximum representable value and one value above it.

requirements.quote: The representation of this number on the wire is: 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F.
requirements.condition: When encoding Remaining Length value 268435455.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F.
requirements.why_checkable: The maximum value's encoding can be compared byte-for-byte.

requirements.quote: The table below shows the Remaining Length values represented by increasing numbers of bytes. Digits From To 1 0 (0x00) 127 (0x7F) 2 128 (0x80, 0x01) 16 383 (0xFF, 0x7F) 3 16 384 (0x80, 0x80, 0x01) 2 097 151 (0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F) 4 2 097 152 (0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x01) 268 435 455 (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F)
requirements.condition: When selecting the encoded width of a Remaining Length value.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 1 byte for 0-127, 2 bytes for 128-16383, 3 bytes for 16384-2097151, and 4 bytes for 2097152-268435455.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary values around each listed interval can be encoded and their widths measured.

requirements.quote: The algorithm for encoding a decimal number (X) into the variable length encoding scheme is as follows: do digit = X MOD 128 X = X DIV 128 // if there are more digits to encode, set the top bit of this digit if ( X > 0 ) digit = digit OR 0x80 endif 'output' digit while ( X> 0 )
requirements.condition: When encoding a decimal Remaining Length value X.
requirements.required_behavior: Repeatedly output X modulo 128, integer-divide X by 128, set the digit's top bit when more digits remain, and continue while X is greater than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoder output for arbitrary values can be compared with the stated deterministic algorithm.

requirements.quote: The algorithm for decoding the Remaining Length field is as follows: multiplier = 1 value = 0 do digit = 'next digit from stream' value += (digit AND 127) * multiplier; multiplier *= 128; while ((digit AND 128) != 0);
requirements.condition: When decoding the Remaining Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize multiplier to 1 and value to 0, add each low-seven-bit digit times the multiplier, multiply the multiplier by 128 after each digit, and continue while the digit's top bit is set.
requirements.why_checkable: Parser results can be compared with the deterministic decoding computation for supplied byte sequences.

requirements.quote: When this algorithm terminates, value contains the Remaining Length in bytes.
requirements.condition: After Remaining Length decoding terminates.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the accumulated value as the Remaining Length in bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: The parser's reported length can be compared with the algorithm's accumulated value.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length encoding is not part of the variable header.
requirements.condition: When classifying or parsing message-header components.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the Remaining Length encoding as outside the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the Remaining Length encoding in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: Parser offsets and component boundaries can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The number of bytes used to encode the Remaining Length does not contribute to the value of the Remaining Length.
requirements.condition: When calculating the Remaining Length value.
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude the bytes occupied by the Remaining Length encoding itself.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Count Remaining Length encoding bytes in the Remaining Length value.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared value can be compared with the bytes following the field, excluding the field's own width.
